news.head: Marsh visits New York
A film made entirely by AI wins audiences, and an argument
news.body: A feature made with AI from script to score is a box-office hit. The actors' and writers' guilds are furious.

news.head: The Super Bowl is the most-watched broadcast of the year
news.body: Parties across the country, and advertisers paying record sums for a few seconds of airtime.

news.head: Marsh visits California
A small town in Louisiana loses its last factory
news.body: The plant that employed half the town is closing. The mayor says they'll find a way to start over.

news.head: Teenagers and their phones: a debate in every household
news.body: Schools in South Dakota are banning phones in class, and parents are trading tips on screen time.

news.head: Drones deliver groceries and prescriptions in the suburbs
news.body: Packages are arriving by air in under thirty minutes in a growing number of towns.

news.head: Rural hospitals in Hawaii are closing
news.body: Three hospitals have shut their doors in two years. Patients must drive hours for care.

news.head: Budget office: the Build More Homes Act will cost $90 billion over ten years
news.body: Adds about 0.22% to output by year three; lowers rents by about 3.3% over five years; it will cost $90 billion over ten years.

news.head: Bitter cold grips the northern states
news.body: Temperatures fell below zero from Montana to Maine. Shelters opened extra beds.

news.head: Air taxis lift off in three cities
news.body: Electric air taxis are flying paying passengers between downtown and the airport in a few big cities.

news.head: AI chatbots move into offices and classrooms
news.body: Companies are using AI to write code and answer customers. Schools are rewriting their rules on homework.

news.head: Astronauts return to the moon
news.body: For the first time in more than half a century, Americans have walked on the lunar surface, near its south pole.

news.head: Marsh visits California
Self-driving trucks begin hauling freight on the interstates
news.body: The first driverless trucks are running on highways in the Southwest. The Teamsters say they're a threat to millions of jobs.

news.head: A new bridge opens in Arizona
news.body: The span replaces a ferry that has run for more than eighty years. Hundreds walked across on opening day.

news.head: Marsh visits California
A county fair in Georgia draws record crowds
news.body: Prize hogs, pie contests and a Ferris wheel. Organizers say it was the best fair in memory.

news.head: Veterans return to a quieter country
news.body: With no war on, veterans in New Jersey are going back to school and starting businesses.

news.head: Marsh visits California
Marsh visits California
A trillion-dollar company that didn't exist ten years ago
news.body: An AI firm founded in a rented office is now worth more than most countries' entire stock markets.

news.head: Spring floods along the rivers of Maine
news.body: Melting snow and heavy rain have pushed rivers over their banks. Families are moving to higher ground.

news.head: Marsh visits California
A community in Minnesota rallies after a flood
news.body: Volunteers are filling sandbags and gutting homes. Churches are serving meals around the clock.

news.head: Astronomers report a new comet
news.body: The comet may be visible to the naked eye next month if it survives its pass near the sun.

news.head: Marsh visits California
March Madness: an underdog shocks a top seed
news.body: Office pools across the country were busted when a small school knocked off one of the favorites.

news.head: Marsh visits California
Rents climb out of reach in Delaware
news.body: Rents in the state's biggest city are up by a quarter in two years. Young people are moving back in with their parents.

news.head: The deficit worries Wall Street
news.body: Bond traders say the government is borrowing too much. Interest rates are creeping up.

news.head: Sports betting apps are everywhere
news.body: Millions of Americans now bet on games from their phones. Counselors say calls to gambling hotlines are up.

news.head: A long-unsolved case is cracked in Nevada
news.body: Detectives say new evidence led them to a suspect decades after the crime.

news.head: Opening day: baseball is back
news.body: Fans filled ballparks across the country. Even in the cold, the stands were full.

news.head: Wages are rising for the lowest-paid workers
news.body: With jobs plentiful, workers are switching employers for better pay, and wages at the bottom are climbing fastest.

news.head: Data centers strain the grid in Maryland
news.body: A new AI campus will use as much power as a city of a million people. Utilities are asking customers to pay for new power plants.

news.head: In the papers: press secretary Michael Rourke's a household employee paid off the books

The president holds a cabinet meeting
Fed holds rates at 3.75–4.00%
Employers add 125,000 jobs in April; unemployment 4.5%

An earthquake rattles California
news.body: The quake knocked items off shelves across the region but caused little serious damage.

news.head: The White House sends its budget to Congress
news.body: Defense +4%, other agencies -6%, taxes -0.3% of GDP; the deficit +0.22% of GDP.

news.head: Prices up 3.0% over the past year
news.body: Food is up 2.8%, shelter 3.8% and medical care 3.5%.

news.head: A hometown hero from South Dakota retires
news.body: After eighteen seasons, the beloved veteran played his last game before a standing ovation.

news.head: The House Energy and Commerce Committee approves the AI Safety Standards Act
The government hits the debt limit
news.body: The Treasury's extraordinary measures last about five months.

news.head: The Kentucky Derby draws a record crowd
news.body: A long shot came from behind to win the run for the roses at Churchill Downs.

news.head: Tornadoes rip through Oklahoma
news.body: A line of storms spun up several tornadoes overnight, flattening homes and barns.

news.head: Marsh visits California
The House passes the AI Safety Standards Act, 375-60
A fusion company puts power on the grid
news.body: A startup's pilot plant has delivered electricity to the grid for the first time. It will be years before fusion power is cheap.

news.head: A jury acquits in a case that gripped Idaho
news.body: After three weeks of testimony, the jury deliberated for two days. The defendant wept as the verdict was read.

news.head: Employers add 57,000 jobs in May; unemployment 4.4%
A novel about a family from Nebraska tops the bestseller lists
news.body: Readers say the story of three generations rings true. Hollywood has bought the rights.

news.head: A new shopping center opens outside Indiana's biggest city
news.body: The developer says it will be the region's largest, with department stores and hundreds of shops.

news.head: Justice Marisol Ortega announces retirement: a vacancy on the Supreme Court
